This blog post discusses the `renv` package and updating R.

# Set-up

You will need the `renv` package and R.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
install.packages("renv") # install renv
library(renv)
```
:::


Check your R version.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
R.version$version.string
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "R version 4.5.2 (2025-10-31)"
```


:::
:::

# Updating R

Mac: manually on CRAN ([https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/)). Then install (opening the `.exe` file you've downloaded in a *place that makes sense and where your computer always knows to look*).

Windows: using the `installr::updateR()` function, for example.

## Updating your lock.file to the new R version

Open an R project and navigate to the `renv` folder. You should see there your previous R version, which is where your projects packages are stored in a lockfile. To transfer these packages over to the new R version, run the following:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
R.version # make sure you're on the new R version
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
renv::status() # check the status; should say there's no renv package
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
install.packages("renv") # install renv
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
renv::status() # should now say there are no packages in the project library
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
renv::restore() # to install packages in the lockfile from old R version
```
:::


You'll be given three options (activate and use the project library; do not activate the project; cancel). Enter '1' to activate and use the project library.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
renv::update() # update all old packages
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
renv::snapshot() # save updated lockfile
```
:::


If you have broken dependencies, you'll be given three options (snapshot without fixing any issues, install and/or update packages and then snapshot, or cancel). In this instance I suggest entering '2' to fix any broken dependencies and taking a snapshot. You'll then be given an overview of the changes that will be made (which will be very long, assuming you have a lot of packages in your lockfile), and asked if you want to proceed. Enter 'Y' to do so.

Finally, check your renv status again.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
renv::status()
```
:::


You will hopefully see the following message.

```
No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state.
```
